root_cause.text: In `drivers/mtd/spi-nor/debugfs.c`, `spi_nor_params_show()` passed `sizeof(snor_f_names)` to `spi_nor_print_flags()` instead of the array element count, so the SPI-NOR debugfs flag-name bounds check used an inflated length and could read past the `snor_f_names` pointer array.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `spi_nor_print_flags(s, nor->flags, snor_f_names, sizeof(snor_f_names));` to `spi_nor_print_flags(..., ARRAY_SIZE(snor_f_names));`, and the commit message explains that `sizeof()` on an array of pointers returns bytes (`element_count * sizeof(void *)`), making `names_len` too large and allowing out-of-bounds access in `spi_nor_print_flags()`.

intent_record.how: This makes the array_size() helper available in this translation unit at compile time, allowing the code to use the macro without relying on indirect inclusion from other headers.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the SPI NOR parameter display to pass the correct flag-name array length to `spi_nor_print_flags()`.
intent_record.what: The call to `spi_nor_print_flags()` in `spi_nor_params_show()` was changed to pass `ARRAY_SIZE(snor_f_names)` instead of `sizeof(snor_f_names)` as the fourth argument, with the call split across two lines.
intent_record.how: This changes the value used to describe the number of flag-name entries from the array's byte size to its element count, so the flag-printing helper receives the correct length and can iterate over the names properly without misinterpreting the size.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in `spi_nor_params_show()`: `spi_nor_print_flags(s, nor->flags, snor_f_names, sizeof(snor_f_names));`. The root cause states that this call should pass the array element count, not `sizeof(snor_f_names)`, because `spi_nor_print_flags()` uses `names_len` in `if (i < names_len && names[i])`, and an inflated length can let it index past the pointer array. There is no corrective handling here (no `ARRAY_SIZE(snor_f_names)` or equivalent), so the bug is present and the fix is not yet applied.
